faq1Q: How do I compress images without visible quality loss?
faq1A: Lower the quality slider (default 75%); the tool shows real-time compressed size and ratio. At quality 80–85, WebP is usually indistinguishable from the original while reducing size by 60%–90%.
faq2Q: How do I compress images to a specific size (e.g., 200KB)?
faq2A: Enable 'Target Size' and enter the target KB (e.g., 200). The tool auto-adjusts quality using binary search to hit that exact size. Ideal for application photos or email/WeChat attachments.
faq3A: Drag multiple images in at once, or paste screenshots with Ctrl+V. All images are compressed in parallel. Download individually or export as ZIP.
faq4Q: Is this image compression tool safe? Will my images be leaked?
faq4A: No. All compression happens locally and works offline. Images never leave your browser — no upload request is ever made.
faq5Q: Does it support WebP / AVIF format conversion?
faq5A: Yes, it converts JPG/PNG to WebP. AVIF encoding may degrade to WebP on some browsers (with a notice).

faq7Q: Can I use compressed images for WeChat / email / websites?
faq7A: Yes. Use 'Target Size' mode to compress within limits (e.g. 200KB/100KB) or switch to WebP for smaller file sizes.
faq8Q: Does image compression help with SEO and loading speed?
faq8A: Yes. Smaller images improve page load time and Core Web Vitals (LCP). Since processing is local, originals are never uploaded — balancing performance and privacy.
